pairs: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron,
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron,
Say to the sons of Israel:
Hæc sunt animalia quæ comedere debetis de cunctis animantibus terræ:
These are the animals that you ought to eat out of all the living things of the earth.
All that has a divided hoof,
and that chews over again, among the cattle,
But whatever certainly chews over again,
but has a hoof that is not divided,
and you shall consider them to be among what is unclean.
The rock rabbit which chews over again,
and whose hoof is not divided,
and so also is the hare,
for it too chews over again,
yet its hoof is not divided,
which, though its hoof is divided,
The flesh of these you shall not eat,
nor shall you touch their carcasses,
because they are unclean to you.
Hæc sunt quæ gignuntur in aquis,
These are the things that breed in the waters,
and which it is lawful to eat.
omne quod habet pinnulas et squamas,
All that has little fins and scales,
tam in mari quam in fluminibus et stagnis,
as much in the sea, as in the rivers and ponds,
Quidquid autem pinnulas et squamas non habet,
But whatever does not have fins and scales,
eorum quæ in aquis moventur et vivunt,
of those things that live and move in the waters,
their flesh you shall not eat,
and their carcasses you shall avoid.
Cuncta quæ non habent pinnulas et squamas in aquis,
All that does not have fins
and scales in the waters shall be polluted.
Hæc sunt quæ de avibus comedere non debetis,
These are those things among the birds which you must not eat,
and which are to be avoided by you:
et milvum ac vulturem juxta genus suum,
and the kite, as well as the vulture, according to their kind,
et omne corvini generis in similitudinem suam,
and all that is of the raven kind, according to their likeness,
and the hawk, according to its kind,
and the plover according to its kind,
Omne de volucribus quod graditur super quatuor pedes,
whatever steps upon four feet shall be abominable to you.
Quidquid autem ambulat quidem super quatuor pedes,
But whatever certainly walks upon four feet,
and also has longer legs behind,
with which it hops upon the earth,
ut est bruchus in genere suo,
such as the beetle in its kind,
each one according to its kind.
Quidquid autem ex volucribus quatuor tantum habet pedes,
whatever has only four feet shall be detestable to you.
et quicumque morticina eorum tetigerit, polluetur,
And whoever will have touched their carcasses shall be defiled,
et erit immundus usque ad vesperum:
and he shall be unclean until evening.
et si necesse fuerit ut portet quippiam horum mortuum,
And if it will be necessary to carry any of these dead things,
et immundus erit usque ad occasum solis.
and he shall be unclean until the sun sets.
Omne animal quod habet quidem ungulam,
Every animal that certainly has a hoof, but which is not divided,
nor does it chew over again,
immundum erit: et qui tetigerit illud, contaminabitur.
And whoever will have touched it shall be contaminated.
Quod ambulat super manus ex cunctis animantibus, quæ incedunt quadrupedia,
Whatever walks upon its hands, out of all the animals that advance on all fours,
qui tetigerit morticina eorum, polluetur usque ad vesperum.
Whoever will have touched their carcasses shall be polluted until evening.
Et qui portaverit hujuscemodi cadavera, lavabit vestimenta sua,
And whoever will have carried this kind of carcass shall wash his clothes,
et immundus erit usque ad vesperum:
and he shall be unclean until evening.
quia omnia hæc immunda sunt vobis.
For all these are unclean to you.
Hæc quoque inter polluta reputabuntur de his quæ moventur in terra,
Likewise, these shall be considered among the polluted things, out of all that moves upon the earth:
the weasel, and the mouse, and the crocodile,
each one according to its kind,
Qui tetigerit morticina eorum, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:
Whoever will have touched their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
et super quod ceciderit quidquam de morticinis eorum,
And anything upon which something from their carcasses will have fallen shall be defiled,
whether it is a vessel of wood,
or anything by which work is done.
et polluta erunt usque ad vesperum,
These shall be dipped in water and shall be defiled until evening,
but then afterwards these shall be clean.
in quod horum quidquam intro cecidit,
into which something from these will fall,
and therefore it is to be broken.
Any of the foods that you eat,
si fusa fuerit super eum aqua,
if water from such a vessel will have been poured upon it,
et omne liquens quod bibitur de universo vase, immundum erit.
And every liquid which one may drink from such a vessel shall be unclean.
Et quidquid de morticinis hujuscemodi ceciderit super illud,
And if anything from among these kinds of dead things has fallen upon it,
et omnis aquarum congregatio munda erit.
and all reservoirs of water shall be clean.
Whoever will have touched their carcasses shall be defiled.
If it falls upon seed grain,
Si autem quispiam aqua sementem perfuderit,
But if anyone has poured water upon the seed grain,
and afterwards it was touched by the carcasses,
If any animals will have died,
from which it is lawful for you to eat,
qui cadaver ejus tetigerit, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:
whoever will have touched its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
et qui comederit ex eo quippiam, sive portaverit, lavabit vestimenta sua,
And whoever will have eaten or carried anything of these shall wash his clothes,
et immundus erit usque ad vesperum.
and he shall be unclean until evening.
Omne quod reptat super terram, abominabile erit,
All that creeps across the earth shall be abominable,
neither shall it be taken up as food.
Whatever advances by four feet upon the chest,
or that drags across the soil,
Do not be willing to contaminate your souls,
nor shall you touch any of these,
Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester:
For I am the Lord your God. Be holy,
quia ego sanctus sum. Ne polluatis animas vestras in omni reptili quod movetur super terram.
Do not pollute your souls with any creeping thing, which moves across the land.
qui eduxi vos de terra Ægypti,
who led you away from the land of Egypt,
so that I would be your God;
Ista est lex animantium ac volucrum,
This is the law of animals
and of every living soul that moves in the waters
ut differentias noveritis mundi et immundi,
so that you may know the difference between clean and unclean,
et sciatis quid comedere et quid respuere debeatis.
and so that you may know what you ought to eat, and what you ought to refuse.
